chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maimun, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muslima al-Jariri, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «He knows that which deceives the eyes» so he said: Do you not see a man; he looks at a thing, and yet, it is as if he does not look at it? That is what deceives the eyes.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah; a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: That which deceives the eyes; hidden glances or looks that betray inner intent
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Exalted and Glorious is He; an honorific title for God

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'kha'inat al-a'yun' (deceives the eyes) mean according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defining 'khayranat al-ayn' as the subtle, involuntary glance that reveals inner desire even when one feigns indifference. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual integrity of the gaze, distinguishing between conscious looking and the 'betrayal' of the eyes by hidden lust or attention. It serves as a practical guide for *muraqaba* (spiritual vigilance) over one's sensory faculties.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Tha’laba bin Maimoun, from Abdul-Rahman bin Maslama al-Jareeri, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,

about the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «He knows that which deceives the eyes» [40:19] so he said: Do you not see a man; he looks at a thing, and yet, it is as if he does not look at it? That is what deceives the eyes.
